answer.generated: In the context of entity-relationship (ER) modeling, generalization represents a logical link between an entity known as the parent entity and one or more entities referred to as child entities. The parent entity is considered more general since it encompasses the child entities as specific cases. This relationship indicates that the child entities are specializations of the parent entity, meaning they represent particular instances or subsets of the broader category defined by the parent entity. Thus, generalization and specialization are complementary concepts where generalization captures the overarching category, while specialization delineates its specific subcategories.
